scope: Static audit only; no inference performed by this audit. Compare actual native server-reported prompt strings with the publisher usage format and advertised task.
findings: Actual system wording, role delimiters, newlines, user transcript and assistant prefix match the publisher raw ChatML example, substituting the advertised clean_punctuate task for the example format_email task. All24 native reported prompts and recorded prompt SHA256 agree.

Publisher tokenizer registers im_start/im_end and repository tokens, but does not register task prefixes as separate special token IDs. They therefore function as ordinary text delimiters under the published tokenizer; parse_special=true does not warrant removing them or inventing new tokens.
Explicit no-automatic-BOS input starts with im_start token, which is itself the published BOS ID1. Native token-ID requests avoid an accidental duplicate im_start.
Publisher supplies worked usage only for format_email and bullet_points; clean_punctuate is advertised in the task list without a corresponding successful worked output or task-specific evaluation.

No mismatch in the implemented published contract was identified. Observed email-template/hallucination failures apply to this exact published Q4 artifact and clean_punctuate condition; they do not prove all formats, precisions, retraining or hypothetical alternate prompts incapable.
